name: Billfisher Sport-Fishing Charters
summary: A family-owned fishing charter business in Bridgetown run by Captain Ralph White and his son, Captain Noah White. They fish from two boats: Billfisher III, a 40 foot Viking sportfisher for shared and private trips, and Take a Chance, a 50 foot Bertram with an air conditioned salon. Trips go after wahoo, mahi, tuna and marlin, and some add a swim, snorkel or BBQ lunch.
standouts: Family-owned, with over 35 years of fishing experience
Two boats: a 40 ft Viking sportfisher for up to 6 and a 50 ft Bertram for up to 12
Inshore grounds about 10 minutes from the dock, offshore within 15 minutes
Guests can take home cleaned fillets from the catch

contact.address: Berthed at the Inner Careenidge, Bridgetown, Saint Michael

trips.title: Shared Half Day Trip
trips.summary: A shared deep sea fishing trip on Billfisher III, a 40 foot Viking sportfisher, with up to six guests. Lines are in the water within about 10 minutes of leaving the dock, fishing inshore or offshore for wahoo, mahi, tuna and barracuda, with a chance of marlin.
highlights: Runs Mondays and Wednesdays in season

trips.title: Fish, Swim & BBQ Adventure
trips.summary: A relaxed private afternoon on Billfisher III that mixes light trolling with a stop at a calm spot to swim and snorkel. The crew grills part of the catch on board for lunch, and a bottle of bubbly marks the day.
highlights: Trolling for mahi, barracuda or tuna
Swim and snorkel stop with turtles and shipwrecks

checkNotes: Online booking through rezbs.com links on each trip (Check Availability); links recorded but not opened. Payments are charged in BBD at US$1 = BBD$2.00, USD shown for reference. Cancellation: at least 72 hours before the trip for a full refund; weather cancellations rescheduled or refunded. Address spelled 'Inner Careenidge' on the contact page (the Careenage). Snorkelling with turtles and shipwrecks is offered on the Platinum charters and the Fish, Swim and BBQ trip; the menu item 'Swim with the Turtles' points to this snorkel add-on, not a separate trip. No turtle feeding is advertised. Guests may bring their own boat-approved rods on private charters only. Footer says Copyright 2025, and photos were uploaded in June 2026.
